entries.name: Structured state space sequence model
entries.definition: A structured linear state-space sequence model whose normal-plus-low-rank state matrix is transformed to diagonal-plus-low-rank form for efficient convolution-kernel computation and recurrent sequence evaluation.
entries.identity_notes: S4 denotes Gu, Goel and Ré's specific structured state-space construction, not every state-space model, S4D, an exponential-smoothing model, or Mamba's input-dependent selective state updates. Deep S4 networks compose these linear models with channel mixing and nonlinearities.
entries.mechanism: Bilinear discretization gives recurrent and zero-initial-state convolutional views. A unitary basis change produces a diagonal-plus-low-rank state matrix; Cauchy-kernel evaluations, a low-rank Woodbury correction and an inverse FFT compute the finite convolution kernel.
entries.locator: Sections 2.1–2.4 and 3.1–3.4, equations 1–5, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 1, PDF/printed pp. 3–7
limitations: This record follows arXiv v3's original diagonal-minus-PQ* parameterization. Section 3.4 notes possible numerical instability with right-half-plane eigenvalues and points to a later diagonal-minus-PP* revision; stability is not asserted unconditionally.
The core S4 model is linear. A deep nonlinear S4 network adds channel mixing and nonlinear transformations; kernel computation is not the complete network.
No universal accuracy, memory or wall-clock advantage is asserted.
entries.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
entries.mapping_rationale: The local concept is a particular parameterized sequence model. AIO Model is broader; a generic neural-network mapping would conflate its linear state-space core with the nonlinear networks built from it.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Proposes a structured parameterization and computation strategy for long-sequence state-space modeling. Its efficiency and benchmark claims are author claims; this record covers the method and explicit stability limitation, not a universal improvement.

entries.name: Hungry Hungry Hippos layer
entries.definition: A sequence layer that combines projected queries, keys and values with shift and diagonal state-space models, using multiplicative interactions to associate and retrieve sequence information.
entries.identity_notes: H3 is the layer defined in Fu and colleagues' Algorithm 1. Networks interleave H3 with MLP layers; the paper's hybrid H3-attention model additionally uses attention layers. Those complete networks and the FlashConv execution algorithm are not identical to this component.
entries.mechanism: Project the input to Q, K and V; pass K through a shift state-space model. Within each head, feed the outer product of shifted keys and values through a diagonal state-space model, multiply by Q, then concatenate heads and apply an output projection.
entries.locator: Section 3.2, Algorithm 1 and the surrounding H3 Layer paragraph, PDF/printed p. 5
limitations: The scalar-head elementwise formula is a special case; general heads use outer products and matrix-vector contractions.
The complete H3 language model and hybrid attention architecture require additional blocks beyond this layer. No universal language-model performance or recall guarantee is asserted.
entries.title: Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models
entries.mapping_rationale: The defining algorithm takes a sequence representation and outputs a transformed representation for subsequent layers. AIO Layer is broader than this specific shift/diagonal state-space construction.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Investigates an expressivity gap between state-space models and attention for language modeling and proposes H3 plus FlashConv. These are different contributions: a sequence layer and an execution algorithm. Only the inspected H3 method is added in this round.

entries.name: Retentive network
entries.definition: An autoregressive neural sequence architecture that stacks pre-normalized residual blocks combining gated multi-scale retention with feedforward transformations, with parallel, recurrent and chunkwise forms of retention.
entries.identity_notes: RetNet denotes Sun and colleagues' architecture, not a generic recurrent network or an attention-based Transformer language model. Its retention operation is a component, while the architecture also specifies gating, normalization, residual paths and feedforward blocks.
entries.mechanism: Retention projects position-modulated queries, keys and values and combines causal query-key interactions with exponential distance decay. Different heads use fixed decay scales; headwise normalization and a swish gate combine their outputs. Recurrent evaluation updates a decayed key-value state, and chunkwise evaluation combines parallel within-chunk interactions with recurrent cross-chunk state.
entries.locator: Sections 2.1–2.3, equations 5–9 and Figures 3–4, PDF/printed pp. 3–5
limitations: Constant recurrent decoding cost is with respect to prior sequence length at fixed model dimensions, not constant total work for a whole sequence or arbitrary model size.

The mathematical parallel, recurrent and chunkwise representations do not by themselves establish identical finite-precision outputs for every implementation; numerical score-normalization details matter.
This record does not generalize the paper's reported benchmark or hardware results.
entries.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
entries.mapping_rationale: Learned retention projections, gates and feedforward transformations compose a neural architecture. ArtificialNeuralNetwork is broader and does not incorrectly identify retention as Transformer attention.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Proposes retention as a sequence mechanism with parallel training, recurrent inference and chunkwise evaluation. The source describes an architecture and evaluated language models; the record does not turn the title or abstract into a general claim of superiority over Transformers.
